proposals.before: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Qiandao (1166) and was appointed salt commissioner of Yanguan.
proposals.after: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Qiandao (1166) and was appointed county defender (wei) of Yanguan.
proposals.reason: 鹽官尉 is the county defender/sheriff (wei), not a salt commissioner; 鹽官 is the place-name Yanguan.

proposals.before: In the second year of Qiandao he became a jinshi and was appointed salt commissioner of Yanguan.
proposals.after: In the second year of Qiandao he became a jinshi and was appointed county defender (wei) of Yanguan.
proposals.reason: Same error: 尉 is not a salt office.

proposals.before: When his wife's parent died he left office for mourning. After mourning he served as a staff officer on the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was briefly transferred to Huaidong, then returned to Jiangdong and was appointed magistrate of Xi'an County.
proposals.after: When his father died he left office for mourning. After mourning he served as a staff officer on the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was briefly transferred to Huaidong, then returned to Jiangdong and was appointed magistrate of Xi'an County.
proposals.reason: 遭外艱 after 丁母憂 is mourning for his father, not a parent-in-law.

proposals.before: He encountered mourning for a parent-in-law; when the mourning ended he served as staff officer of the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was moved to Huaidong, then returned to his former post, and was changed to magistrate of Xi'an County.
proposals.after: He encountered mourning for his father; when the mourning ended he served as staff officer of the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was moved to Huaidong, then returned to his former post, and was changed to magistrate of Xi'an County.
proposals.reason: 外艱 denotes paternal mourning, not a parent-in-law.

proposals.before: The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuiyou invited him to join his staff as a counselor, but he declined and was instead appointed a staff officer in the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
proposals.after: The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuoyou invited him to join his staff as a counselor, but he declined and was instead appointed a staff officer in the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
proposals.reason: 袁說友 is Yuan Shuoyou; Shuiyou misreads 說.

proposals.before: The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuiyou invited him into his staff as counselor, but he did not accept and was changed to staff officer of the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
proposals.after: The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuoyou invited him into his staff as counselor, but he did not accept and was changed to staff officer of the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
proposals.reason: Same name-reading error for 說友.

proposals.before: The crown prince obtained a copy of Lou Ji's "Expanded Characters for the Thousand-Character Classic" and was especially pleased with it. He ordered Dai Xi to write a colophon.
proposals.after: The crown prince obtained a copy of Lou Ji's "Expanded Ganlu Characters" and was especially pleased with it. He ordered Dai Xi to write a colophon.
proposals.reason: 廣幹祿字 continues the Ganlu character-book tradition (干祿字), not the Thousand-Character Classic (千字文).

proposals.before: The heir apparent obtained a copy of Ji's work "Expanded Characters for the Thousand-Character Classic" and was especially pleased, ordering Dai Xi to write a colophon for it.
proposals.after: The heir apparent obtained a copy of Ji's work "Expanded Ganlu Characters" and was especially pleased, ordering Dai Xi to write a colophon for it.
proposals.reason: Same misidentification of 幹祿字 with the Thousand-Character Classic.

proposals.before: How are the isolated and poor to be extended?
proposals.after: How are the isolated and poor to get ahead?
proposals.reason: 伸 here means to have an opening for advancement, not physical extension.

proposals.before: In the ninth month he sacrificed at the Bright Hall and served as ritual commissioner.
proposals.after: In the ninth month, at the Bright Hall sacrifice, he served as ritual commissioner.
proposals.reason: 為禮儀使 marks his office at the rite; he is not said to have performed the sacrifice himself.

proposals.before: Made intendant of the Dongxiao Palace, he returned home and soon died. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with an additional posthumous promotion to Special Advancement.
proposals.after: Made intendant of the Dongxiao Palace, he returned home and soon died. He was posthumously granted the rank of Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with an additional posthumous promotion to Special Advancement.
proposals.reason: 贈 here is a posthumous rank, not a territorial enfeoffment.

proposals.before: During the construction of Gaozong's mausoleum, the temporary quarters of the various offices required endless supplies of food and wine. Shen Huan urgently told the pacification commissioner Zheng Ruhe, "The state is in deep mourning, yet officials feast and make merry as usual. How can that be right?"
proposals.after: During the construction of Gaozong's mausoleum, the temporary quarters of the various offices required endless supplies of food and wine. Shen Huan urgently told the pacification commissioner Zheng Ruxie, "The state is in deep mourning, yet officials feast and make merry as usual. How can that be right?"
proposals.reason: 汝諧 is Ruxie, not Ruhe; the visible English spelling misreads 諧.

proposals.before: Thereupon those who used the occasion to commit wrongdoing were punished, those who pursued repayment and extortion were pursued for compensation, and expenditures abruptly decreased.
proposals.after: Thereupon those who used the occasion to commit wrongdoing were punished, those who had extorted levies were made to repay them, and expenditures abruptly decreased.
proposals.reason: 追償率斂者 are the extortionists made to make restitution, not officials pursuing repayment.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion and given the special posthumous title Duanxian (Upright and Law-abiding).
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted the office of direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion and given the special posthumous title Duanxian (Upright and Law-abiding).
proposals.reason: 追贈 of a pavilion academician post is a posthumous office, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Appointed magistrate of Lizhou, he had not yet taken office when Xue Shusi, pacification commissioner of Jinghu and Hubei, invited him to serve as chief confidential secretary.
proposals.after: Appointed magistrate of Lizhou, he had not yet taken office when Xue Shusi, pacification commissioner of Jinghu, invited him to serve as chief confidential secretary.
proposals.reason: 京湖 is the Jinghu theater, not Jinghu and Hubei as two separate regions.

proposals.before: He was appointed magistrate of Lizhou but had not yet taken up the post when Xue Shusi pacified Jinghu and Hubei and invited him as chief confidential secretary.
proposals.after: He was appointed magistrate of Lizhou but had not yet taken up the post when Xue Shusi, as pacification commissioner of Jinghu, invited him as chief confidential secretary.
proposals.reason: 宣撫京湖 names Xue's office; it does not say he personally 'pacified' Jinghu and Hubei.

proposals.before: He memorialized rewards for Guan as Gentleman of Loyal Achievement and registrar of Hanchuan, posthumously enfeoffed Zhongsheng as Gentleman of Martial Cultivation, and gave offices to two of his descendants.
proposals.after: He memorialized that Guan be appointed Gentleman of Loyal Achievement and registrar of Hanchuan, posthumously granted Zhongsheng the title Gentleman of Martial Cultivation, and gave offices to two of his descendants.
proposals.reason: 贈 is a posthumous rank grant, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary, but Right Rectifier Zheng Zhao objected and the appointment was shelved.
proposals.after: He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary, but Right Rectifier of Speech Zheng Zhaoxian objected and the appointment was shelved.
proposals.reason: 鄭昭先 is Zheng Zhaoxian; Zhao drops the given-name graph 先.

proposals.before: He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary; because right rectifier Zheng Zhao spoke first, the appointment was shelved.
proposals.after: He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary; because Right Rectifier of Speech Zheng Zhaoxian spoke against it, the appointment was shelved.
proposals.reason: 言 here is remonstrance, not 'spoke first'; 昭先 is the personal name.

proposals.before: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and acting vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, he was made designated drafter of the Baomo Pavilion and magistrate of Chengdu.
proposals.after: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and acting vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, he was made edict attendant of the Baomo Pavilion and magistrate of Chengdu.
proposals.reason: 待制 is the edict-attendant literary-post title, not 'designated drafter'.

proposals.before: He next said, "Take the openness of the Qingli and Yuanyou eras as your model, and the silencing of dissent in the Shaosheng, Chongning, and Guanning eras as your warning.
proposals.after: He next said, "Take the openness of the Qingli and Yuanyou eras as your model, and the silencing of dissent in the Shaosheng, Chongning, and Daguan eras as your warning.
proposals.reason: 崇、觀 abbreviates 崇寧 and 大觀 (Chongning and Daguan), not a 'Guanning' era.

proposals.before: He next said: "One should take Qingli and Yuanyou listening to words as the model, and take Shaosheng, Chongning, and Guanning taboo on words as the warning.
proposals.after: He next said: "One should take Qingli and Yuanyou listening to words as the model, and take Shaosheng, Chongning, and Daguan taboo on words as the warning.
proposals.reason: 崇、觀 is Chongning and Daguan; 'Guanning' is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: Made intendant of the Chongfu Palace, he soon died. He was granted retirement as academician of the Huawen Pavilion with the rank Grandee of Court Discussion and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee of Court Submission.
proposals.after: Made intendant of the Chongfu Palace, he soon died. He was granted retirement as academician of the Huawen Pavilion with the rank Grandee of Court Discussion and was posthumously granted the rank Grandee of Court Submission.
proposals.reason: 贈宣奉大夫 is a posthumous rank, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: The county comprised thirteen townships and suffered bandit raids at irregular intervals. The pacification commissioner transferred his office and took charge of the prefecture as well. He first memorialized to remit grain rent for two years in eight townships, and an edict was issued accordingly.
proposals.after: The county comprised thirteen townships and suffered bandit raids at irregular intervals. The pacification commissioner transferred his office and took charge of the prefecture as well. The pacification commissioner first memorialized to remit grain rent for two years in eight townships, and an edict was issued accordingly.
proposals.reason: 初奏 is the pacification commissioner's memorial, not Fan Yingling's; 'He' wrongly suggests Yingling.

proposals.before: Then he abolished village clerks’ requisitions, checked registration fraud, and within a few months the provincial register was completed. He submitted this register along with seed-tax regulations to the general fiscal office, and from then on tax and corvée duties were equalized.
proposals.after: Then he abolished village clerks’ requisitions, checked registration fraud, and within a few months the abridged registers were completed. He submitted these registers along with seed-tax regulations to the general fiscal office, and from then on tax and corvée duties were equalized.
proposals.reason: 省簿 is the reduced/corrected household ledger, not a provincial register; 省 here means to simplify, matching the idiomatic county ledger.

proposals.before: He at once set out, taking his parents with him.
proposals.after: He at once set out, taking his remaining parent with him.
proposals.reason: The preceding unit already records mourning for his mother (丁內艱); 奉親 after that death refers to the surviving parent, not both parents.

proposals.before: Thereupon he took his parents and set out.
proposals.after: Thereupon he took his remaining parent and set out.
proposals.reason: Chinese 親 after 丁內艱 is the surviving parent; rendering it as plural parents contradicts the mothers already recorded death.

proposals.before: He did not exchange letters and gifts with superiors, nor did he currying favor with powerful families in recommendations; he acted according to office, and none dared obstruct him with improper means.
proposals.after: He did not exchange letters and gifts with superiors, nor did he curry favor with powerful families in recommendations; he acted according to office, and none dared obstruct him with improper means.
proposals.reason: did he currying favor is ungrammatical; the verb must be curry.

proposals.before: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, diarist, and attendance gentleman, he memorialized on entering office, “A ruler should observe the boundary between principle and desire.”
proposals.after: Promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, diarist, and attendance gentleman, he memorialized on entering office, “A ruler should observe the boundary between principle and desire.”
proposals.reason: 宗正少卿 is the Court of the Imperial Clan, not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (太常).

proposals.before: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, diarist, and court gentleman for attendance, he entered memorial: “One who rules others should keep to the boundary between principle and desire.”
proposals.after: Promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, diarist, and court gentleman for attendance, he entered memorial: “One who rules others should keep to the boundary between principle and desire.”
proposals.reason: Same 宗正/太常 confusion as in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: He was promoted to vice minister of punishments while concurrently receiving edicts, then to left tutor and grand tutor of the crown prince. For three years he guided the Eastern Palace, expounding the classics and offering counsel as occasions arose.
proposals.after: He was promoted to vice minister of punishments while concurrently supervising secretary, then to left tutor and grand tutor of the crown prince. For three years he guided the Eastern Palace, expounding the classics and offering counsel as occasions arose.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is the office of supervising secretary, not a generic ‘receiving edicts’.

proposals.before: Promoted to vice minister of punishments while concurrently receiving edicts, then elevated to left tutor and grand tutor of the crown prince; for three years he instructed the Eastern Palace, expounding the classics and offering guidance as occasions arose.
proposals.after: Promoted to vice minister of punishments while concurrently supervising secretary, then elevated to left tutor and grand tutor of the crown prince; for three years he instructed the Eastern Palace, expounding the classics and offering guidance as occasions arose.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 給事中 as ‘receiving edicts’.

proposals.before: Whenever the crown prince attended the emperor, Jingsun always reported everything they had discussed, and the emperor invariably expressed approval.
proposals.after: Whenever the crown prince attended the emperor, he always reported everything that had been lectured and heard, and the emperor invariably expressed approval.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太子入侍，必以其所講聞悉奏之 takes the crown prince as the one reporting instruction; the idiomatic line invents Jingsun as the reporter.

proposals.before: Granted the title academician of the Duanming Hall, he lived in retirement for ten years, then died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
proposals.after: Granted the title academician of the Duanming Hall, he lived in retirement for ten years, then died and was posthumously granted the rank of Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
proposals.reason: 贈金紫光祿大夫 is a posthumous rank, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Chen Maolian, whom Jingsun had recommended as public-fields official and assigned to Jiaxing, upon hearing that Jingsun had left office said: I cannot fail Master Xu.”
proposals.after: Chen Maolian, whom Jingsun had recommended as public-fields official and assigned to Jiaxing, upon hearing that Jingsun had left office said: “I cannot fail Master Xu.”
proposals.reason: The literal English drops the opening quotation mark before the cited speech.

proposals.before: The commentary says: Alas — was Ningzong as ruler, or Han Tuozhou as chief councilor, truly a time for launching war?
proposals.after: The commentary says: Alas — with Ningzong as ruler and Han Tuozhou as chief councilor, was this truly a time for launching war?
proposals.reason: The source coordinates 寧宗之為君 with 韓侂胄之為相; the literal ‘or’ splits them into alternatives.

decisions.reason: 授鹽官尉 appoints him county defender (尉) of Yanguan (鹽官); 鹽官 is the place-name, not a salt office.

decisions.reason: 宣撫京湖 is the Jinghu theater as one command, not Jinghu and Hubei as two regions.

decisions.reason: 贈仲升修武郎 is a posthumous rank grant, not an enfeoffment.

decisions.reason: 寶謨閣待制 is edict attendant of the Baomo Pavilion, not designated drafter.
